caption_or_description: Top view of iron filings sprinkled around a magnet tracing a pattern of magnetic field lines. Interestingly, the magnetic field lines continue inside the magnet (not revealed by the filings) and form closed loops.

When the compass needle is not aligned with the magnetic field (left), the oppositely directed forces on the needle produce a pair of torques (called a couple) that twist the needle into alignment (right).
The magnetic field patterns for a pair of magnets. (a) Opposite poles are nearest each other, and (b) like poles are nearest each other.
A microscopic view of magnetic domains in a crystal of iron.
